from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Strange Setup: A Counting Mystery", 
            [
                'Imagine two blocks on a frictionless floor.', 
                'A small block sits between a wall and a large block.', 
                'The large block slides in, starting a chain of collisions.'
            ]
        )
        
        # Define Colors
        COLOR_FLOOR = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_SMALL = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_LARGE = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_WALL = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_FLOOR))
        
        # Floor and Wall
        # Floor is at the bottom of the grid
        floor_y = self.grid["F1"][1] - 0.5
        floor = Line(
            [self.grid["F1"][0] - 0.5, floor_y, 0], 
            [self.grid["F6"][0] + 0.5, floor_y, 0], 
            color=COLOR_FLOOR
        )
        wall = Line(
            [self.grid["A1"][0] - 0.5, self.grid["A1"][1] + 0.5, 0], 
            [self.grid["F1"][0] - 0.5, floor_y, 0], 
            color=COLOR_WALL, 
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        self.play(Create(floor), Create(wall))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_SMALL)
        )
        
        # Small block (m) - Green
        small_block = Square(side_length=0.6, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=COLOR_SMALL, stroke_color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(small_block, "F2")
        small_block.set_y(floor_y + 0.3) # Sit on floor
        m_label = Text("m", slant=ITALIC, color=WHITE).scale(0.8).next_to(small_block, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Large block (M) - Blue
        large_block = Square(side_length=1.2, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=COLOR_LARGE, stroke_color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(large_block, "F5")
        large_block.set_y(floor_y + 0.6) # Sit on floor
        M_label = Text("M", slant=ITALIC, color=WHITE).scale(0.8).next_to(large_block, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(small_block), FadeIn(m_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(large_block), FadeIn(M_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_LARGE)
        )
        
        # 1. Large block slides in (M slides left)
        slide_distance = 1.5
        self.play(
            large_block.animate.shift(LEFT * slide_distance),
            M_label.animate.shift(LEFT * slide_distance),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # 2. Collision 1: M hits m
        collision_pt1 = small_block.get_right()
        self.play(Flash(collision_pt1, color=WHITE, flash_radius=0.4))
        
        # m flies left, M slows slightly (Visual representation)
        self.play(
            small_block.animate.shift(LEFT * 1.0),
            m_label.animate.shift(LEFT * 1.0),
            large_block.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.2),
            M_label.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.2),
            run_time=0.6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # 3. Collision 2: m hits Wall
        collision_pt_wall = [wall.get_x(), small_block.get_y(), 0]
        self.play(Flash(collision_pt_wall, color=WHITE, flash_radius=0.4))
        
        # m bounces back towards M
        self.play(
            small_block.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.4),
            m_label.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.4),
            large_block.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.1),
            M_label.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.1),
            run_time=0.4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Precise fix for FileExistsError: [Errno 17] File exists: 'media/texts'
        text_dir = pathlib.Path("media/texts")

        except Exception:
            pass

        # BASE

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_str, lecture_points):
        """Custom method to setup the visual layout of the scene."""
        # Replaced Title(title_str) with Text(title_str).to_edge(UP) to avoid LaTeX dependency
        self.title = Text(title_str).to_edge(UP)
        self.lecture = VGroup(*[
            Text(point, font_size=28) 
            for point in lecture_points
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).to_edge(LEFT).shift(UP * 0.5)
        
        # Define a grid system for positioning
        self.grid = {
            "D1": LEFT * 4 + DOWN * 2,
            "D2": LEFT * 2 + DOWN * 2,
            "D3": ORIGIN + DOWN * 2,
            "D5": RIGHT * 4 + DOWN * 2,
        }

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, coord_key):
        """Custom method to position mobjects based on the grid keys."""
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[coord_key])

    def construct(self):
        # Configuration
        title_str = "The Collision-Pi Connection"
        lecture_points = [
            "- Elastic Collisions",
            "- Conservation of Momentum",
            "- Kinetic Energy Exchange",
            "- Digit Calculation of π"
        ]

        # 1. Setup Layout
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_points)

        # 2. Visual Representation (Bouncing Blocks)
        # Create a simplified grid system for the right side
        block_small = Square(side_length=0.6, fill_opacity=1, color=BLUE)
        block_large = Square(side_length=1.2, fill_opacity=1, color=RED)
        
        # Position using the custom grid
        self.place_at_grid(block_small, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(block_large, "D5")

        # 3. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(self.title))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture, shift=RIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(Create(block_small), Create(block_large))
        
        # Simple collision animation
        self.play(
            block_large.animate.move_to(self.grid["D3"]),
            block_small.animate.move_to(self.grid["D1"]),
            run_time=1.5,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # Labeling
        label_m = Text("m", font_size=24).next_to(block_small, UP)
        label_M = Text("M", font_size=24).next_to(block_large, UP)
        
        self.play(Write(label_m), Write(label_M))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the scene layout with bullet points
        lines = [
            '- Every hit moves the point by a fixed arc length.',
            "- The total path spans exactly half the circle's circumference.",
            '- As the mass increases, the step size gets smaller.',
            '- This lets us fit more steps into the same arc.',
            '- The number of steps calculates the value of Pi.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Angle of Pi: Why the Counting Works", lines)
        
        # Define constants and colors
        COLOR_THETA = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_PI = "#FFFFFF"
        initial_theta = 0.6  # Initial visual theta
        small_theta = 0.2    # Representing larger mass
        circle_radius = 1.8

        # Persistent Circle
        circle = Circle(radius=circle_radius, color=GREY_E)
        self.place_in_area(circle, "B2", "E5")
        dot = Dot(circle.point_at_angle(0), color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_THETA))
        self.play(Create(circle))
        
        # Arc and Theta Label
        arc1 = Arc(radius=circle_radius, start_angle=0, angle=initial_theta, color=COLOR_THETA)
        arc1.move_to(circle.get_center())
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        theta_label = Text("θ", color=COLOR_THETA, font_size=24)
        label_pos = circle.get_center() + 2.2 * np.array([np.cos(initial_theta/2), np.sin(initial_theta/2), 0])
        theta_label.move_to(label_pos)
        
        self.play(Create(arc1), FadeIn(theta_label))
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(initial_theta)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_THETA)
        )
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text using Unicode symbols
        theta_eq = Text("θ = arctan(√(m/M))", color=COLOR_THETA, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(theta_eq, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        semi_circle_bg = Arc(radius=circle_radius, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        semi_circle_bg.move_to(circle.get_center())
        
        self.play(Write(theta_eq))
        self.play(Create(semi_circle_bg))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_THETA)
        )
        
        new_arc = Arc(radius=circle_radius, start_angle=0, angle=small_theta, color=COLOR_THETA)
        new_arc.move_to(circle.get_center())
        
        new_label_pos = circle.get_center() + 2.1 * np.array([np.cos(small_theta/2), np.sin(small_theta/2), 0])
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(arc1, new_arc),
            theta_label.animate.move_to(new_label_pos).scale(0.8),
            dot.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(small_theta))
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_THETA)
        )
        
        # Fill semi-circle
        num_arcs = int(PI / small_theta)
        arcs = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, num_arcs):
            a = Arc(radius=circle_radius, start_angle=i*small_theta, angle=small_theta, color=COLOR_THETA)
            a.move_to(circle.get_center())
            arcs.add(a)
        
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(a) for a in arcs], lag_ratio=0.1, run_time=2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_PI)
        )
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text using Unicode symbols
        final_eq = Text("Collisions = ⌊π/θ⌋", color=COLOR_PI, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(final_eq, "F2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text using Unicode symbols
        pi_label = Text("π radians", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_label, "D1", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Write(final_eq), FadeIn(pi_label))
        self.wait(2)

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define layout
        title = "Conclusion: Physics as a Computer"
        lines = [
            "This simple system acts as a mechanical computer for Pi.",
            "It reveals a deep link between dynamics and geometry.",
            "Mathematical beauty emerges from the simplest physical laws."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors for lines
        COLOR_1 = "#ADD8E6" # Light Blue
        COLOR_2 = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_3 = "#FFFFFF" # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_1))
        
        # Setup visual elements: Wall, Blocks, Counter
        wall = Line(
            self.grid["B1"] + UP * 0.5, 
            self.grid["E1"] + DOWN * 0.5, 
            color=WHITE, 
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        small_block = Square(side_length=0.6, fill_opacity=0.8, color=COLOR_1, fill_color=COLOR_1)
        self.place_at_grid(small_block, "C2")
        
        large_block = Square(side_length=1.2, fill_opacity=0.8, color=BLUE_E, fill_color=BLUE_E)
        self.place_at_grid(large_block, "C4")
        
        counter_label = Text("Collisions:", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_label, "A2")
        
        count_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # FIXED: Replace Integer(0) with Text("0") to avoid LaTeX dependency error ('latex' not found)
        counter_val = Text("0", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_val, "A4")
        
        # Update counter based on tracker using Text and become()
        counter_val.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(
            Text(str(int(count_tracker.get_value())), font_size=36, color=WHITE).move_to(self.grid["A4"])
        ))

        self.add(wall, small_block, large_block, counter_label, counter_val)

        # Animation: Fast-forward collision counter
        small_origin = small_block.get_center().copy()
        large_origin = large_block.get_center().copy()
        shake_small = lambda m: m.move_to(small_origin + RIGHT * 0.05 * np.sin(self.renderer.time * 50))
        shake_large = lambda m: m.move_to(large_origin + LEFT * 0.02 * np.sin(self.renderer.time * 10))
        
        small_block.add_updater(shake_small)
        large_block.add_updater(shake_large)
        
        self.play(
            count_tracker.animate.set_value(3141592),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        small_block.remove_updater(shake_small)
        large_block.remove_updater(shake_large)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_2))
        
        # Highlight counter in green
        self.play(
            counter_val.animate.set_color(COLOR_2).scale(1.2),
            counter_label.animate.set_color(COLOR_2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_3))
        
        # Fade out interaction elements
        fade_group = VGroup(wall, small_block, large_block, counter_label, counter_val)
        
        # FIXED: Replace MathTex(r"\pi") with Text("π") to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        pi_symbol = Text("π", font_size=180, color=COLOR_3)
        self.place_in_area(pi_symbol, "B2", "E5")

        self.play(
            FadeOut(fade_group),
            FadeIn(pi_symbol, shift=UP * 0.5)
        )
        
        self.play(pi_symbol.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=1.5, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Collision-Pi Connection: Why Bouncing Blocks Compute Pi
outline.target_audience: High school physics students and undergraduate mathematics enthusiasts

sections.title: The Strange Setup: A Counting Mystery
sections.content: Introduce the physical system: a frictionless floor, a fixed wall on the left, a small block (mass m), and a large block (mass M) sliding in from the right. We count every 'clack' (collision) between blocks and between the small block and the wall.
sections.example: Visualize a tiny hamster in a small box (1kg) and a massive elephant in a large box (100kg) sliding toward each other. When the elephant hits the hamster, and the hamster hits the wall, we count the total bounces.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Laws of the Game
sections.content: Explain perfectly elastic collisions using two fundamental laws: Conservation of Momentum (mass times velocity) and Conservation of Energy (kinetic energy). These two equations define how the velocities change after every hit.
sections.example: Graphical overlay showing the equations: m*v1 + M*v2 = Constant (Momentum) and 1/2*m*v1^2 + 1/2*M*v2^2 = Total Energy.

sections.title: The Pattern Emerges: Scaling the Mass
sections.content: Show what happens when we increase the mass ratio in powers of 100. If M = 1kg and m = 1kg, we get 3 collisions. If M = 100kg, we get 31 collisions. If M = 10,000kg, we get 314 collisions.
sections.example: An animation showing the 'clacks' speeding up as the mass ratio increases. 1:1 ratio -> 3 clacks; 1:100 ratio -> 31 clacks; 1:1,000,000 ratio -> 3,141 clacks. The digits of Pi appear!

sections.title: The Geometry of Velocity: Mapping to a Circle
sections.content: Transform the physics into geometry. By rescaling the velocity axes (using the square root of the masses), the Conservation of Energy equation becomes the equation of a circle: x² + y² = R². Every collision is a jump from one point on the circle to another.
sections.example: A coordinate system where the x-axis is 'Velocity of small block' and the y-axis is 'Velocity of big block'. As collisions occur, a point traces steps around the perimeter of a circle.

sections.title: The Angle of Pi: Why the Counting Works
sections.content: Explain that each collision corresponds to a fixed-size arc on the circle. The total number of collisions is the number of times this arc fits into the semi-circle (Pi radians). As the big block's mass increases, the arc angle becomes smaller, allowing for more precise 'steps' along the curve.
sections.example: A visual showing a circle being 'sliced' into tiny even pieces. The number of pieces represents the number of collisions. The total length of the 'path' is exactly Pi.

sections.title: Conclusion: Physics as a Computer
sections.content: Summarize how a simple physical interaction acts as a mechanical computer for calculating one of the most fundamental constants in mathematics. Emphasize the beauty of how disparate fields like dynamics and geometry intersect.
sections.example: A final shot of the blocks hitting 3,141,592 times as the mass ratio becomes astronomical, with the symbol π glowing in the background.

storyboard.title: The Strange Setup: A Counting Mystery
lecture_lines: Imagine a frictionless floor with a wall on the left.
A small block and a massive block sit nearby.
The large block slides in, starting a chain of collisions.
animations: Create a horizontal line (#FFFFFF) for the floor and a wall [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg] at the left edge.

Add a small green block [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] (mass m, #00FF00) and a large blue block [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] (mass M, #0000FF) to the right of the wall.

The large blue block [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] moves left, striking the small green block [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg]; use a flash effect (#FFFFFF) for every collision.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Laws of the Game
lecture_lines: Momentum is conserved as the blocks push each other.
Kinetic energy is also preserved in these elastic bounces.
These two laws define the outcome of every collision.
animations: Display the Conservation of Momentum equation: 'm v_1 + M v_2 = \text{const}' in yellow (#FFFF00) accompanied by the blocks icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blocks.svg].
Display the Conservation of Energy equation: '1/2 m v_1^2 + 1/2 M v_2^2 = E' in cyan (#00FFFF).
Highlight both equations with a white rectangle (#FFFFFF) to indicate they are the governing laws.

storyboard.title: The Pattern Emerges: Scaling the Mass
lecture_lines: With equal masses, we count exactly three collisions.
At a hundred-to-one ratio, thirty-one collisions occur.
Increasing the mass further reveals a startling pattern.
The count perfectly matches the digits of Pi.
This mechanical system actually computes the constant Pi.
animations: Show a simulation with M=1 and m=1; the collision count '3' appears in white (#FFFFFF) above the blocks.
Show M=100 and m=1; the collision count increments to '31' in white (#FFFFFF).
Show M=10,000 and m=1; the collision count increments to '314' in white (#FFFFFF).
Flash the digits '314' in pink (#FF00FF) to emphasize the connection to Pi.
Display the symbol 'pi' (#FF00FF) as the mass ratio increases further to 1,000,000.

storyboard.title: The Geometry of Velocity: Mapping to a Circle
lecture_lines: We map these velocities onto a geometric plane.
Rescaling the axes transforms our equations into a circle.
Energy conservation keeps the system on this circle's edge.
Each block-to-block collision is a jump along the circle.
Wall collisions reflect the point across the vertical axis.
animations: Draw coordinate axes labeled v1 and v2 in grey (#888888).
Update axis labels to x = sqrt(m)v1 and y = sqrt(M)v2 using white text (#FFFFFF).
Draw a cyan circle (#00FFFF) centered at the origin, representing the conservation of energy.
A point representing the system's state jumps to a new position on the circle for each collision between blocks [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg].
The point reflects across the y-axis for each collision between the small block [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] and the wall.

storyboard.title: The Angle of Pi: Why the Counting Works
lecture_lines: Every hit moves the point by a fixed arc angle.
This angle depends on the ratio of the masses.
The point travels along the perimeter of the circle.
We count how many steps fit into half the circle.
The final count reveals the digits of Pi.
animations: Highlight a single arc segment on the circle and label its angle as 'theta' (#FFFF00).
Show the relationship theta = arctan(sqrt(m/M)) in yellow text (#FFFF00).
Animate the circle filling up with arcs of size theta, starting from the positive x-axis.
Show that the total number of steps is the number of times theta fits into the semi-circle (pi radians).
Display the final equation: 'Number of collisions = floor(pi / theta)' in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Conclusion: Physics as a Computer
lecture_lines: This system acts as a mechanical computer for Pi.
It reveals a deep link between dynamics and geometry.
Mathematical beauty emerges from the simplest physical laws.
animations: Animate a fast-forward of the block simulation [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/computer.svg] with a massive mass ratio, with the collision counter spinning rapidly.
The counter stops at '3,141,592', which is highlighted in green (#00FF00).
Fade out the blocks and equations, leaving only the large symbol 'pi' (#FFFFFF) center-stage.
